changelog.title: Builds that rise into the drops

groups.name: Added
items: A build in the three bars before each drop: a hand-drum roll that accelerates (8ths, 16ths, then 32nds into the stop), tunes up a fifth and opens out in stereo; her own chop as the riser, the drop's first note repeating faster and climbing a fourth, taking over the moment she stops singing; and the talking bass teasing the drop on its chord in the stop bar. Everything stops dead at the stop, so the silence before the drop stays.

groups.name: Changed
items: Why, measured: the bars before each drop sagged instead of building (drop 1: bars 22-24 at -19.1, -17.3, -18.8 LUFS, falling). Now they rise: -18.2, -14.9, -14.7, into the drop at -11.8. Before drop 2 she sings almost to the stop, so the roll stays 0.7x under her (her voice 12.6 dB over it) and comes up after her last word: bar 48 now -12.3 LUFS, rising into the drop, where it fell to -16.9.
The band's muffled-to-open sweep into each drop starts at 900 Hz instead of 450: still a lift, no longer a hole. The build itself is left out of the sweep, because it is what rises.

groups.name: Changed
items: The drops' mid-bass is now a Surge XT bass played like a performer, replacing the distorted contrabass pizzicato (two hits a bar, the weakest genre element). Surge renders in 5.8 ms steps and its filter (the "vowel") and wavefolder are set between steps, so every note carries a gesture: a "wow" that opens and closes, a "yoy" wobbling at 32nds, a stab, a rise, a fall, a chewing growl. Each 4-bar phrase goes call, answer, talk, fill, between the kicks; drop 2 plays hardest.

Sound: two saws (one an octave down) into a West Coast wavefolder and a resonant OB-Xd low-pass; after it a gentle high-pass at 70 Hz (the clean mono sub owns the bottom), an OTT-style three-band squash, and width above 400 Hz only. Its notes follow the chord (octave and fifth snap to the bar's chord).

Mix, measured: the mid-bass now exists between 300 Hz and 2.5 kHz in the drops (her chops were 26-36 dB over it there, now 10-16 dB): present, still under her. It ducks up to 5 dB while her chops sound; her vocal margin stays within 0.6 dB of v5.1.

changelog.title: Film VFX from Surge XT; a cleaner mix

groups.name: Added
items: Trailer-grade sound design synthesised with Surge XT (free, open-source, Serum-class), through AIWaves' synth engine: a braam + sub drop + impact on each drop's downbeat (about -6 dB against the mix there: huge, the groove survives), Doppler whooshes flying left-to-right into the drops and right-to-left out of them (-16 dB), an impact on her peak (-11 dB), tuned glitch shards through the drops (-26 dB), an evolving drone under the space intro and outro (-15 dB), and a long low braam with the last hit.
Stems: `LONGING_STEMS=1` writes each group (vocal, drums, bass, zither, handpan, chops, strings, choir, story, vfx) for analysis.

groups.name: Changed
items: Mix, measured: her voice was already on top while she sings (+6 to +9 dB in her body), but only +0.6 dB at 1.6-3.2 kHz, where the strings sat. The strings now dip ~4 dB at 250 Hz and 2.5 kHz while she sings: her margin there is +2.4 dB. The monk layer gets a low cut. Mono check (phone speakers): nothing cancels; the widest layer, the choir, loses 2.8 dB.

changelog.title: A film behind the song (Tripp St.)

groups.name: Added
items: A cinematic story runs behind the music, scene by scene, made only of real recordings (sample-pi CC0 textures, NASA public-domain audio), far back: low-passed for distance, in a hall, slowly moving. Intro: space (a shuttle far away, a lunar surface). Verse 1: night on earth (a haunted hum, a glass hum, one crow far left). Into drop 1: a dark whoosh circling into the downbeat. Drop 1: distant sonic booms under the crashes. Verse 2: a memory (a piano, reversed, far away). Drop 2: a cinematic boom. Outro: the shuttle recedes, back in space.
Ear-candy transients: glass pings tuned to each bar's chord, between the beats (one every 4 bars in verse 1, two per bar in the drops).
Levels: the background 20-24 dB under the mix, the impacts about 16 dB under: felt, never in her way.
The render now writes `arrangement.json`: every note, hit and vocal piece it placed (the AIWaves arrangement view draws it).

groups.name: Added
items: Ghost notes: soft snare taps between the main hits wherever the groove plays.
Drops: offbeat hi-hats (an open hat every 4th bar), darbuka flams, and a crash on each drop's downbeat. The drops gained 3 dB of top end above 6 kHz.
Phrase-aware fills: the 4th bar of each phrase alternates a bongo run with a tom cascade (high to low, ending on the deep drum).

groups.name: Changed
items: The bass varies: the bounce alternates octave and fifth, and every 4th bar it plays a syncopated pattern locked to the toms' 3-3-2.

changelog.title: No uncut singing: alien and spiritual

groups.name: Changed
items: Every line is cut into breathing pieces: each of her notes found (pitch + level), passing notes under 0.55 s dropped, each kept note sounds for 3/4 of its length with a soft 120 ms fade, then a breath. Pieces stay exactly where she sang them, so they still land on her chords and beat. 51 pieces, the longest 3.1 s; her doubles are cut with the same mask.
Each piece keeps its whole line's level (no per-piece normalising), so her dynamics survive the cuts.

groups.name: Added
items: Alien: every breath holds a frozen cloud of the note she just sang, drifting around the head (-10 dB under her).
Spiritual: an octave-down "monk" (-16 dB) and an octave-up "angel" (-18 dB) ghost of her voice.
A choir under the intro, verses and outro: her longest A and E stretched about 8x (Paulstretch) into a breathing pad, with an octave-down copy.

changelog.title: Her vocals arranged end to end; a psychedelic zither

groups.name: Changed
items: The whole vocal track is arranged, not just placed. Intro: her final "D C B A", reversed, far back; then her first words from take 1 (right) answered by take 2 (left). Verse 1: one intimate voice. Drop 1: the hook, then she returns inside the drop (phrase 3's first half, then her ending). Verse 2 and the last line: doubled with her other take. Drop 2: her emotional peak ("A A A ... C B") as the climax.

Real double-tracking: she sang every line twice, so the second take sits under the first, split left/right at -6 dB, aligned note by note (dynamic time warping, then stretched piece by piece between notes). Same note at the same time: 81-84% (76% when only stretched). Phrase 7's other take turned out to be a different melody (51%), so it stays single.
Every fragment lands on the chord she originally sang it over (the drops reuse her verse chords bar for bar).

The zither's space: a tape echo with slow wow, a filter on the echoes that breathes open and shut every two bars, a reverse swell into each phrase, and an octave shimmer. The plucks themselves stay clean.

groups.name: Added
items: Vocal tape-stops: her last note before each drop slows to a halt in the stop.
Reversed vocal pickups: each hook call is sucked in by its own first note, backwards.
Drop 2: a half-speed (octave-down) shadow of her hook under it.

groups.name: Removed
items: The intro chop teasers (her reversed ending and first words do that job now).

groups.name: Added
items: The player has a side panel with this changelog and the song's git history (`scripts/aiwaves_export.py` builds it).
The song is under version control on branch `wip/longing`: script, analysis, stems (LFS), the render (LFS) and the player.
`scripts/analyze_longing.py` rebuilds her beat grid, chords and vocal chops from the stems; verified identical to the files used.
`aiwaves/PLAN.md`: the plan for AIWaves, an agent-first DAW with a read-only live view for humans.

changelog.title: Zither lead, her chops as the hook

groups.name: Changed
items: Lead instrument: the flute is replaced by the dan tranh (Vietnamese zither). Why: a sustained wind fought her sustained voice in the same space; plucks ring and leave room, and the zither is a signature colour of this genre. Short notes are plucked, held notes use the left-hand bend, very long notes use tremolo.
Form: intro, verse 1, drop 1, verse 2 (phrases 5-6), drop 2, outro (phrases 7-8). Two drops instead of one long one.
Glitch fills: every 16 bars instead of 8, half a beat instead of a beat, no low thump, at half level. Her vocal stutters are at half level and darker. Why: they hit too hard.

groups.name: Added
items: Her vocal chops: 52 single sung notes are cut from her a cappella and tuned exactly to each chord. They form the drops' hook: she calls "aah - ah - aaah" and the zither answers. In drop 2 she harmonises herself.
Handpan rolls the chord tones between the hook and the zither in the drops.
Intro teasers: two long notes of hers before verse 1.
A stop and a muffled-to-open filter build before both drops.

groups.name: Added
items: A real string section (VSCO-2 cellos and violas) plays her chords under her, voice-led bar to bar. Why: the verses were thin in the middle.
The shaker, darbuka slaps and bongos circle the listener (one turn every two bars).
The band opens from muffled to full over the two bars before the drop.

groups.name: Changed
items: The verses' drums and bass step back, so the drop jumps +2.4 dB instead of +1.6 dB.

groups.name: Changed
items: Tempo 140 → 80 BPM, her own tempo. Each phrase is fitted onto the bar grid tracked from the piano she sang to (stretch 0.970–1.007, inaudible). Why: at 140 her phrases floated across the beat.
Harmony: the bass and lead follow her chords bar by bar (mostly Am–G, with F and Em), read from her piano part.
Drums: glitch-hop backbeat (snare on 2 and 4), lighter under her, full in the drop.

groups.name: Added
items: The flute answers only in the gaps she leaves; the drop's flute theme is built from her own melody ("A A G D E").
Her first note, frozen into a pad, opens the song.

groups.name: Added
items: Around her clear dry voice, made only from her own voice: detuned chorus doubles, a reverse-reverb swell into every phrase, frozen clouds circling the head after each phrase, dotted-8th echo throws, glitch stutters on two phrase ends, an octave-and-fifth shimmer.

groups.name: Added
items: Mono sine sub on the chord roots with glides, ducking under every deep drum hit; contrabass growl stabs; half-time snare; Tipper-style glitch fills; dotted-8th ping-pong on the flute.

groups.name: Added
items: Madam Snowflake's "Longing" a cappella over flute and tribal drums (140 BPM). The music moved to A minor to match her; every pitched drum is tuned to the key.

commits.author: Hermes Agent
commits.subject: Longing v5.2: a talking bass (Tipper / CloZee), sent live to AIWaves
commits.body:
- tipper_bass.py: Surge XT played like a performer. It renders in 5.8 ms steps
  and sets the filter ("vowel") and wavefolder between steps, so each note
  carries a gesture (wow, yoy, stab, rise, fall, growl). Phrases run call,
  answer, talk, fill between the kicks. Then a 70 Hz high-pass (the mono sub
  owns the bottom), an OTT-style 3-band squash, and width above 400 Hz.
  This replaces the distorted pizzicato growl in the drops; it ducks under
  her chops.
- Measured: the drops' mid-bass now exists between 300 Hz and 2.5 kHz (chops
  over it: 26-36 dB -> 10-16 dB); her vocal margin is within 0.6 dB of v5.1.
- aiwaves_live.py + export: a running AIWaves app gets each new version as
  live commands (knobs turn, devices and clips appear, the render loads),
  never by overwriting its files.

Her whole performance is cut at its natural seams and re-arranged across the
song (reversed ghost, take-1/take-2 call and answer, lines inside the drops,

commits.subject: Longing v2.1: song, analysis, player with changelog/git panel
commits.body:
Psychedelic world bass built around Madam Snowflake's a cappella "Longing"
(ccMixter, CC BY 3.0): dan tranh lead, handpan, her vocal-chop hook, strings,
tuned tribal kit, sub + growl, at her own tempo (80 BPM) and chords (A minor).

- scripts/make_longing_song.py renders the song; scripts/analyze_longing.py
  rebuilds her beat grid, chords and chops (verified identical).
- The player gets a side panel (changelog + git history) fed by
  scripts/aiwaves_export.py.
- aiwaves/PLAN.md: plan for an agent-first DAW (plan only).
- Stems and the render are stored with LFS; instrument sample libraries are not
  committed (sources in samples/LICENSES.md).
